item.title: This Week In Food: New Diner Food on Polk
item.description: A new diner debuts on Polk, Cenaduria Elvira makes a splash in Oakland's Jack London Square, and the Chronicle reviews Dingles Public House, all in This Week in Food.

item.title: The Internet Can’t Get Enough of the Bushes from Bad Bunny’s Super Bowl Halftime Show
item.description: Bad Bunny took the world by storm during his Super Bowl Halftime Show, and so did the 400 mostly local performers in the now-famous “grass bunny” costumes who are sharing their experiences all over the internet, with one performer listing the prized costume on eBay for $5,000.

item.title: Newsom and California Sue Trump Administration Again, This Time Over Greenhouse Gas Emissions
item.description: Trump’s EPA is running roughshod over all California’s environmental protections, so the state is suing to keep as many of them as intact as possible, the latest being our rollback of how much greenhouse gases can be emitted into the environment.

item.title: Day Around the Bay: MC Hammer Jumps Aboard Honorary Black History Month Cable Car
item.description: Amazon ended its deal with Ring after that creepy Super Bowl commercial; the Vallaincourt Fountain preservationists have filed a lawsuit pausing demolition; and MC Hammer made an appearance on a Black History Month cable car.

item.title: Saturday Links: San Francisco Tech Company Launches $8,000 Laundry-Folding Robot
item.description: Asian American communities are celebrating the Lunar New Year across the Bay Area; an SUV driver wearing a boot cast crashed into a Santa Rosa store; and a new $8,000 laundry-folding robot will fold most clothing and small linens.

item.title: Sam Smith Channels Chaka Khan, George Michael, and Bonnie Raitt In Castro Residency
item.description: The great Sam Smith seemed wistful, grateful, and dare we say happy during their almost 90-minute set Friday night, and you can hear them paying tribute to generations of R&B and soul singers in multiple numbers.

item.title: Field Notes: 124-Year-Old Light Bulb, UC Davis’ Cheeto the Cat, and ‘Trash Falcons’ Art Exhibit
item.description: This week: Hip-hop at Yoshi’s, coastal trails, national park sweethearts, and a Muni beer crawl. Plus, turning Lake Merritt trash into art, repairing bikes for kids, a light bulb that never goes out, and the big cat on campus.

item.title: Ghirardelli Workers Hold One-Day Strike on Valentine’s Day at SF’s Fisherman’s Wharf
item.description: Ghirardelli workers took part in a one-day strike at the company’s flagship location at San Francisco’s Fisherman’s Wharf Saturday demanding a new contract that includes wage increases and preserving their union-run health plan, for which they’ve been bargaining for months.

item.title: Sunday Links: Local Investor Under Investigation for Allegedly Trafficking at Least Ten Women
item.description: The Bay Area is getting hit with several days of solid rain; Assemblymember Diane Papan is working to close a loophole that allows e-bikes to operate at excessive speeds; and a social-climing local entrepreneur has been dubbed “the Epstein of the West.”

item.title: Surf Legend from Prominent Santa Cruz Surfing and Farming Family Killed in Costa Rica Home
item.description: Kurt Van Dyke, a well-known surfer from a prominent Santa Cruz family of surfers who also own Van Dyke Farms in Gilroy, was killed by armed intruders Saturday in his home on Costa Rica's Caribbean Coast where he was a longtime hostel owner.
